parts.label: (i)
parts.answer: The tangents meet at $(3,3)$, which lies on $y=x$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $y=\frac x2+\frac6x=4\to x=2$ or $6$ — B1 B1. Guidance: Inspection or guesswork OK. $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac12-\frac6{x^2}$ — B1. Guidance: Unsimplified OK. When $x=2$, $m=-1\to x+y=6$; when $x=6$, $m=\frac13\to y=\frac13x+2$ — *M1. Guidance: Correct method for either tangent. Attempt to solve simultaneous equations — DM1. Guidance: Could solve BOTH equations separately with $y=x$ and get $x=3$ both times. $(3,3)$ — A1. Guidance: Statement about $y=x$ not required. Total: 6.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: EITHER: $V=(\pi)\int\left(\frac{x^2}{4}+6+\frac{36}{x^2}\right)(dx)$ — *M1. Guidance: Integrate using $\pi\int y^2dx$ (doesn’t need $\pi$ or $dx$). Allow incorrect squaring. Not awarded for $\pi\int\{4-(\frac x2+\frac6x)\}^2dx$. Integration indicated by increase in any power by 1. Integration $\to\frac{x^3}{12}+6x-\frac{36}{x}$ — A2,1. Guidance: 3 things wanted —1 each error, allow $+C$. (Doesn’t need $\pi$.) Using limits “their 2” to “their 6” $(53\frac13\pi,\frac{160}{3}\pi,168\text{ awrt})$ — DM1. Guidance: Evidence of their values $6$ and $2$ from (i) substituted into their integrand and then subtracted. $48-(-\frac{16}{3})$ is enough. Volume for line: integration or cylinder $(\to64\pi)$ — M1. Guidance: Use of $\pi r^2h$ or integration of $4^2$ (could be from $\{4-(\frac x2+\frac6x)\}^2$). Subtracts $\to10\frac23\pi$ oe (e.g. $\frac{32}{3}\pi$, $33.5$ awrt) — A1. OR: $V=(\pi)\int[4^2-(\frac x2+\frac6x)^2](dx)$ — M1 *M1. Guidance: Integrate using $\pi\int y^2dx$ (doesn’t need $\pi$ or $dx$). Integration indicated by increase in any power by 1. $=(\pi)\int[16-(\frac{x^2}{4}+6+\frac{36}{x^2})](dx)$. $=(\pi)[16x-(\frac{x^3}{12}+6x-\frac{36}{x})]$ — A2,1. Guidance: Or $[10x-\frac{x^3}{12}+\frac{36}{x}]$. $=(\pi)(48-37\frac13)$ — DM1. Guidance: Evidence of their values $6$ and $2$ from (i) substituted. $=10\frac23\pi$ oe (e.g. $\frac{32}{3}\pi$, $33.5$ awrt) — A1. Total: 6.
